title: NOAA seasonal hurricane outlook ranges stated as 70% likely contained 58% of Atlantic and eastern Pacific outcomes in 2003-2025, mainly because the ranges are narrower than count noise allows
abstract: Question: are the NOAA seasonal hurricane outlooks calibrated? Each outlook gives ranges for named storms, hurricanes, major hurricanes and ACE that NOAA states have a 70% probability, and probabilities for above-, near- and below-normal seasons. Method: we transcribed 74 archived outlooks (2002-2026) from NOAA CPC pages and Internet Archive copies and verified them against HURDAT2, with a plan written before scoring. Primary sample: 69 outlooks in 2003-2025 (46 Atlantic May and August, 23 eastern Pacific May), 276 range forecasts. Results: the ranges contained 57.6% of outcomes (season-block bootstrap 47.2-67.6%); Atlantic 59.8%, eastern Pacific 53.3%, ACE 47.8% in both basins. The widths cause most of the gap. If NOAA knew the true seasonal mean exactly, the stated count ranges could reach on average 64% coverage with Poisson noise (69% with dispersion measured about observed peak-season SST); observed count coverage was 61%. NOAA's own ACE log errors (0.48 Atlantic, 0.41 eastern Pacific) imply 45% and 58% coverage for the issued widths; observed 48%. NOAA ACE centres were as accurate as a regression on observed SST predictors. After 2013 the Atlantic ranges became wider and coverage rose from 48% to 71%; across 16 basin-era-metric groups coverage followed the width limit (r = 0.73). Since 2014, 31% of range forecasts were below the outcome and 3.5% above it. Season-type probabilities had no clear miscalibration (ranked probability skill against 20-year climatology +0.10 Atlantic, +0.22 eastern Pacific, intervals include 0). Poisson intervals around NOAA midpoints gave 77% count coverage and a 6% better interval score. Provisional 2026: Atlantic hurricanes and ACE fell below the August ranges; eastern Pacific major hurricanes and ACE (338% of median) exceeded the May ranges. Limitations: 46 basin-seasons, hand transcription, HURDAT2 instead of operational values, and Atlantic hurricane counts under-dispersed about the SST predictors, which weakens the width explanation for hurricanes and major hurricanes.

display.caption: Coverage of the NOAA 70% ranges in 2003-2025 by metric and basin (points, 95% season-block bootstrap intervals). Black bars: the highest coverage that the stated widths can give if the seasonal mean were known exactly, with count dispersion measured about observed SST predictors. Dashed line: the stated 70%.

(a) Observed coverage against oracle coverage for each basin, era and metric; points follow the 1:1 line (r = 0.73). Atlantic ranges became wider after 2013 and coverage increased. (b) Direction of misses: after 2014 the outcome was above the range in 31% of range forecasts and below it in 3.5%.

Atlantic May (blue) and August (green) likely ranges and observed seasonal totals, 2003-2026. Open orange circles: outcome outside at least one range. 2026 values are provisional (operational best tracks to 11 November 2026).
